hero.heading: Sanatana Dharma Explained
hero.description: Sanatana Dharma is the ancient spiritual philosophy of India that explains life, purpose, karma, and liberation. Discover its teachings through the Vedas, Upanishads, and Bhagavad Gita in a simple and practical way.

sections.title: What is Sanatana Dharma?
sections.content: Sanātana Dharma, often translated as the “eternal way,” is not merely a religion but a timeless framework guiding human life toward harmony with cosmic truth. Rooted in Vedic wisdom, it emphasizes universal principles—Dharma (righteous duty), Karma (action and consequence), Moksha (liberation), and the pursuit of truth. It teaches compassion, non-violence, respect for all beings, and reverence for nature as divine. Unlike rigid dogma, it adapts across ages, cultures, and contexts, offering a living philosophy of balance, self-realization, and unity. Sanātana Dharma ultimately affirms that existence itself is sacred, and life’s purpose is realizing oneness with the eternal.

sections.title: Sanatana Dharma Explained in Simple Terms
sections.content: Sanatana Dharma teaches that every action has consequences (karma), every person has a duty (dharma), and the ultimate goal of life is freedom from suffering (moksha). It encourages self-realization, compassion, and balance between material and spiritual life.

sections.title: 🌿 Core Principles of Sanatana Dharma
sections.content: The core principles of Sanātana Dharma are eternal guidelines for righteous living and spiritual realization. Dharma teaches duty, truth, and harmony with cosmic order. Karma reveals the law of cause and effect, urging mindful action. Atman signifies the immortal soul, while Brahman is the infinite reality; realizing their unity leads to liberation. Moksha, freedom from rebirth, is the highest goal. The Purusharthas—Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksha—balance ethics, prosperity, desire, and liberation. Rooted in the Vedas and Upanishads, these principles remain timeless, inspiring humanity to live with compassion, wisdom, and balance, bridging ancient insight with modern life.

sections.title: Main Scriptures of Sanatana Dharma
sections.content: The teachings of Sanatana Dharma come from ancient scriptures that explain philosophy, ethics, and spirituality in depth. The Sacred Scriptures are revered texts that embody divine wisdom, guiding humanity toward truth, virtue, and liberation. They are not merely historical records but living sources of spiritual light, offering timeless principles for righteous living. Scriptures preserve revelations, hymns, and teachings that inspire devotion, discipline, and self‑realization. They connect seekers with the eternal, reminding us of the sacredness of existence and the unity of all beings. Through stories, philosophy, and moral codes, they nurture compassion, faith, and inner strength. The Sacred Scriptures ultimately serve as bridges between the human and the divine, illuminating the eternal path of harmony.

items.description: A practical guide to life, duty, and spiritual growth through the dialogue of Krishna and Arjuna.

items.description: Epic stories that teach dharma, devotion, and moral values.

sections.title: Why Sanatana Dharma Matters Today
sections.content: Sanātana Dharma matters today because it offers timeless wisdom for modern challenges. Rooted in universal values of truth, compassion, and harmony, it transcends religion to guide humanity toward ethical living and spiritual balance. In an age of rapid change, its principles—Dharma, Karma, and Moksha—remind us of responsibility, mindful action, and liberation beyond material pursuits. It nurtures inclusivity, respect for diversity, and reverence for nature, aligning with sustainable living. By bridging ancient insight with contemporary needs, Sanātana Dharma inspires resilience, peace, and unity, showing that eternal truths remain relevant in shaping a just, compassionate, and balanced world.

home.ourfourcoreyugassubtitle: The eternal and universal way of life based on truth, righteousness, and spiritual principles that uphold cosmic order. These numbers are not random. They are derived from a base unit of 432,000, multiplied proportionally (4: 3: 2: 1). One Full Day of Brahma: Lifetime of Brahma - 100 Brahma years - Each year = 360 days - Each day = 4 yugas (ages) - Total = 311,040,000,000 human years.

questions.question: What is the difference between Sanatana Dharma and Hinduism?
questions.answer: Sanatana Dharma is the original eternal philosophy, while Hinduism is a modern term used to describe related traditions.

questions.question: Is Sanatana Dharma a religion?
questions.answer: It is more than a religion. It is a way of life and a philosophical system guiding human existence.

questions.question: What is the goal of life in Sanatana Dharma?
questions.answer: The ultimate goal is moksha, or liberation from the cycle of birth and rebirth.
